newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Daewoo Motor raises car export forecast.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Daewoo Motor raises car export forecast.

text.p: Daewoo Motor Co, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Group, has raised its export forecast to 430,000 vehicles in calendar 1997 from an earlier projection of 400,000, the company chairman said on Thursday.
Chairman Kim Tae-gou said three new passenger car models introduced since last November and a strong yen would help increase Daewoo's car exports.
"Dealers overseas have responded positively to our new model cars," Kim said in an interview. "They are competitive both quality-wise and price-wise."
Daewoo's finished car exports totalled 352.900 vehicles last year.
"I'm confident we will post a net profit of 80 billion won this year on sales of about 6.8 trillion won," Kim said.
The projections compare with a 50.3 billion won net profit and a turnover of 4.3 trillion won last year.

Kim said he expected profits to rise despite an economic slowdown in South Korea. "We had earlier expected local sales to total 480,000 units but we have lowered the figure to 450,000 units," he said.
He said new subcompact Lanos and compact Nubira and Leganza models had also helped Daewoo Motor increase its local market share to about 35 percent from last year's 25 percent.
"I think local car sales will pick up in the second half of this year in line with a recovery in the economy," he added.
Kim said his company would ship more than 20,000 cars to the United States in the fourth quarter of this year to resume marketing there.

Daewoo agreed to stay out of the U.S. market until the end of 1995 as part of an agreement ending its 15-year partnership with General Motors Corp in 1992. Kim put Daewoo's U.S. sales at 50,000 cars next year and between 100,000 and 150,000 cars in the year 2000.
